name: Lipsync
summary: A photo speaks a voice track: LTX-2.5 image-and-audio to video, with an optional prompt and prompt rewriting, in any aspect ratio.

source.notes: Converted with tools/import_workflow.py. VHS_LoadAudioUpload is replaced by core LoadAudio, so the whole uploaded clip is used instead of a 10 s window at 65 s; the workflow's own switches stay: text-to-video bypasses the photo path, and prompt enhancement swaps the raw prompt for TextGenerateLTX2Prompt (qwen4-e2b over the LTX text encoder). Resolution is the template's ResolutionSelector: an aspect ratio and a megapixel budget, sides rounded to 32.

inputs.label: Voice
inputs.help: The speech to lipsync to. It is trimmed to the clip's length (see Seconds).

inputs.label: Photo
inputs.help: The face to animate. Leave empty and turn on "Text to video" for a scene made from the prompt alone.

inputs.label: Text to video
inputs.help: On: the photo is bypassed and the clip comes from the prompt only. Off: the photo is the first frame.

inputs.label: Prompt
inputs.default: She looks at the camera, holds her gaze level and says the line. The camera does a single slow push-in; her hair and the fabric move with the wind.
inputs.help: What happens in the shot. Spoken words go in quotes; the voice itself comes from the audio.

inputs.label: Rewrite the prompt
inputs.help: Sends the prompt through qwen first, as the workflow does: a fuller description, one more model pass.

inputs.label: Negative
inputs.default: pc game, console game, video game, cartoon, childish, ugly
inputs.help: What the shot must not look like.

inputs.label: Resolution (MP)
inputs.help: Total pixels of the clip, sides rounded to 32: 0.8 MP is 1152x640 at 16:9. The template's default; higher is sharper and much slower.

inputs.label: Seconds
inputs.help: Length of the clip, and how much of the voice track is used.

credits: Gemma 4 by Google (Gemma Terms of Use)
notes: Image-and-audio to video: the photo is the first frame and the audio track is the voice, so the mouth follows the recording. The prompt says what happens around the line (a pushed-in camera, the hair moving); the words themselves come from the audio, not from the prompt. Rewrite sends your prompt through qwen first, as the original workflow does; turn it off to see your own words unchanged. Format and megapixels are the workflow's ResolutionSelector: 0.8 MP by default, sides rounded to 32. The clip length is the workflow's own duration in seconds, not the audio's, so a 30 s recording gives the first 5 s unless you raise it.
